summary: Validated worker resource observations exposed repeated browser base payloads, a digest-validated native cache eliminated 100% of warm base and adapter fetch payloads at T1 and 91.5M parameters, both native checkpoints stayed below 2.19e-7 relative L2, and both one-step profiles improved frozen TinyStories held-out loss. The 91.5M warm one-shot process spent 2.963 seconds revalidating and initializing versus 1.653 seconds computing, selecting persistent process/model reuse before quantization or mapped offload.

guardrails.detail: T1 and T2 checkpoint relative L2 values were 1.2317732405376926e-7 and 2.1866353039878446e-7, both below 1e-6.
T1 held-out mean loss improved by 0.0006135702133178711 and T2 improved by 0.0033478736877441406 after one adapter step.
All four native assignments produced validated reports; public aggregates exposed observed runtime memory but no device-capacity or JS-heap-limit fields.
Two real authenticated Burn CPU/WASM assignments populated compute, payload, worker-memory, and coordinator-storage cards and retained 1.6795715402185043e-6 checkpoint relative L2.

findings.label: Warm native cache removes immutable artifact fetches
findings.description: The second isolated native process reported zero model and adapter payload bytes at both T1 and T2 while still revalidating the digest-named cached tensors.

findings.label: Resource and numerical contracts scale to 91.5M parameters
findings.description: The unchanged authenticated assignment, telemetry, aggregation, evaluation, and checkpoint paths completed at T2 with 147,456 trainable adapter values and 2.19e-7 relative L2.

findings.label: One-shot native startup dominates warm compute
findings.description: At T2, full cache revalidation plus model initialization consumed 2.963 seconds, 1.79 times the 1.653-second warm gradient compute. Persistent process/model reuse is therefore the next throughput target.

findings.label: Base-only int8 has a bounded T2 memory ceiling
findings.description: The 366,190,504-byte FP32 base was 20.97% of observed 1,746,419,712-byte peak process RSS, so an idealized fourfold base compression could reduce this measured peak by at most 15.73% before runtime overheads.

findings.label: Payload sizes are not packet-level transfer measurements
findings.description: Browser values measure response bodies delivered through Fetch and cannot distinguish browser HTTP-cache hits; coordinator result sizes are exact request bodies. The dashboard now labels this distinction explicitly.

limitations: All measurements came from one Windows host over loopback; they do not establish heterogeneous WAN throughput or remote participant reliability.
The T1 and T2 bases are deterministic randomly initialized research models. Positive one-step held-out movement is a guardrail result, not evidence of useful language-model adaptation quality.
Warm-cache proofs use separate one-shot native processes sharing one local cache, representing repeated work on one volunteer installation rather than cache sharing across different machines.
Peak process RSS is runtime-wide and includes Python/PyTorch overhead; it does not isolate tensor residency by layer.
The profile remains complete FP32 CPU residency after loading. It does not yet prove quantized frozen-base execution, mapped/NVMe offload, GPU placement, or a model larger than system RAM.
Browser payload sizes do not distinguish HTTP-cache hits from network responses and exclude packet/header overhead.
